subject: Clarify: no-model-learning commitment, prompt/response ownership & evidence pack
messages:
From: Lucia Ramos <lucia.ramos@healexa.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Healexa Legal <legal@healexa.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: No-training commitment & ownership for prompts/responses — evidence needed

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Healexa is interested in moving forward but we need to close a few items on privacy and rights before we can start the pilot. Can you confirm the following and provide evidence where possible?

1) No-model-learning (no-training) commitment
   - Can Redwood commit that Healexa traffic will not be used to improve or train models?
   - If yes, what controls/safeguards are in place operationally and contractually?

2) Prompt/response ownership and derivatives
   - Confirmation that prompts and generated responses are treated as customer data and that Healexa retains output IP/ownership rights.
   - Any standard contract language you propose for this.

3) Subprocessor inventory & residency
   - A current inventory of subprocessors with country of processing and whether they have access to raw prompts/response data or only telemetry.

4) Onshore routing / KMS options
   - Options for routing/processing within the US (or EU) and support for customer-managed KMS or onshore HSM.

5) Evidence pack / artifacts
   - Examples of the logs or artifacts Redwood can provide as proof (audit log snippets, SFTP transfer receipts, toggle state evidence showing "no-learn" flag disabled for the customer).

We know some vendors provide an "evidence pack" (subprocessor CSV + example audit log + annotated DPA). We'd like to see what Redwood can deliver within a week so our legal & security team can sign off.

Would prefer a short call with your legal/ops folks tomorrow or Wednesday afternoon (PDT) to walk through.

Thanks,
Lucia Ramos
Head of IT Security — Healexa
lucia.ramos@healexa.com
+1 415-555-0147

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Ramos <lucia.ramos@healexa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: No-training commitment & ownership for prompts/responses — evidence needed

Hi Lucia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Dev (infra/ops) plus David (privacy) so we can respond with both contract language and an operational evidence plan. Quick plan from my side:

- We can provide an annotated DPA draft that includes a firm no-training clause and an explicit output-ip section.
- Ops can produce the subprocessor inventory + an "evidence packet" (audit log sample, SFTP receipt + hash, and a toggle snapshot showing no-learn disabled).
- We support routing to specific regions and can outline KMS options (customer-managed KMS + onshore HSM path).

Proposed next steps:
1) We will send the annotated DPA + evidence checklist by end of day today.
2) Dev will outline the steps to generate the artifacts and an ops timeline (ETA 48 hrs).
3) If that looks good to you, schedule a 30-min call Wednesday 3pm PDT to walk through and agree timelines.

Marissa/Dev/David — can you confirm you can deliver the items above and whether there are any blockers?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Ramos <lucia.ramos@healexa.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 13:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: No-training commitment & ownership for prompts/responses — evidence needed

Hi Lucia / Aditya —

I drafted an annotated DPA that includes:
- A No-Model-Learning clause (we commit not to use Healexa data to train, fine-tune, or adapt models used for other customers).
- Explicit Output IP section confirming customer ownership of prompts and generated responses, with a license back to Redwood solely for providing the service (narrow, non-transferable).
- Subprocessor and cross-border transfer disclosures; we can add an explicit onshore-only processing exhibit for Healexa if required.

Attachments I will share: redwood-dpa-annotated.docx (contains suggested contract language + negotiation notes).

Evidence requested from ops (Dev) that I recommend including as part of our response:
- Subprocessor inventory CSV (processor name, function, country, access level to PII/prompts).
- An audit log snippet tied to a sample request (timestamped, request id, route, model variant, routing policy).
- A signed confirmation of the "no-learn" toggle state for the account from the ops team (timestamped snapshot).
- KMS residency options and what data is encrypted with customer-managed keys vs platform keys.

Litigation/long-term risk note: the proposed Output IP language keeps Healexa-owned outputs with a service-use license back to Redwood that is limited to debugging, support, and fulfilling the service — not for model training. If Healexa prefers absolute assignment of outputs we can discuss, but that has operational and archive implications.

I'll attach the doc to the evidence packet after Dev confirms the ops artifacts are ready.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucia Ramos <lucia.ramos@healexa.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: No-training commitment & ownership for prompts/responses — evidence needed

Thanks — technical ops summary and what we can produce:

1) No-learn operational control
   - We have a per-account "no_learn" toggle in the serving layer. When set, the request/response traffic is excluded from internal telemetry pipelines used by model improvement jobs.
   - Evidence: we can provide a signed toggle snapshot (JSON with account id, toggle name, timestamp) and a short video/gif of the admin console showing the toggle state.

2) Subprocessor inventory
   - We will export subprocessor_inventory.csv (columns: name, role, country_of_processing, access_level). For Healexa we can mark which subprocessors have zero access to raw prompts.

3) Audit logs / sample artifacts
   - We can deliver an anonymized audit log snippet for a sample request id (contains timestamp, route, model, backend host id, and routing decision) and an SFTP transfer receipt if you want files dropped to your SFTP endpoint.

4) Onshore routing & KMS
   - Options: (a) route inference to Redwood US-only pool; (b) route via partner region in EU (if requested); (c) support for customer-managed KMS (we can integrate your AWS KMS key via cross-account IAM) — HSM-backed on-prem KMS requires a short integration project.
   - Evidence: network egress logs and KMS key ARN proof.

5) Timeline & artifacts
   - I will produce the CSV + audit snippet + toggle snapshot by EOD tomorrow (2027-04-06). The evidence_checklist.pdf will describe where each artifact came from and how to verify it.

Attachments (will be included in the evidence packet):
- subprocessor_inventory.csv (export)
- evidence_checklist.pdf (artifact index and verification steps)

Operational caveat: we can enforce no-learning at the point of ingestion, but downstream backups and long-term telemetry pipelines will be explicitly excluded in the evidence we provide. We'll include a note in the packet describing retention policy for these exclusions.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Lucia Ramos <lucia.ramos@healexa.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Healexa Legal <legal@healexa.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: No-training commitment & ownership for prompts/responses — evidence needed

Aditya / Marissa / Dev — thank you, this looks good.

We appreciate the annotated DPA and the ops checklist. The proposed artifacts should be sufficient for initial legal/security review. Two quick asks before the call:

- Please include an example audit snippet that shows how a request id is marked as excluded from model improvement.
- For subprocessor_inventory.csv, can you include a column "access_to_raw_prompts" with boolean values? That will speed our review.

Call confirmed: Wednesday 7 Apr 2027 at 15:00 PDT (Lucia, Healexa Legal; Aditya, Marissa, Dev, David) — calendar invite to follow.

Looking forward to the packet.

Best,
Lucia
